docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Streamlit library that ships a ready-to-use client reporting UI. It fetches data from the Frequenz reporting API, applies the energy reporting utilities from frequenz-lib-notebooks, and renders dashboards, tables, and plots with reusable Streamlit components.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Pre-built Streamlit app with navigation, landing page, and reporting view.
  • Connects to the Frequenz reporting API to fetch microgrid measurements.
  • Ready-made dashboards (metrics, plots, and tables) powered by frequenz-lib-notebooks.
  • Reusable components (sidebar filters, charts, tables) for your own pages.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Install the library (Python 3.12): 
    pip install "frequenz-cs-reporting"
  2. Provide environment variables (see below). A .env file works with Streamlit: 
    REPORTING_API_URL=https://your-reporting-endpoint
FREQUENZ_API_KEY=your-api-key
FREQUENZ_API_SECRET=your-signing-secret
MICROGRID_CONFIG_DIR=toml_directory/
  3. Add .toml files to the toml_directory.
  4. Run the bundled UI from the repo root: 
    streamlit run app.py
    Use the sidebar to pick a microgrid, date range, timezone, and resolution.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
• REPORTING_API_URL (required): Base URL for the Frequenz reporting API.
  • FREQUENZ_API_KEY and FREQUENZ_API_SECRET (required): Credentials used to authenticate and sign Reporting and Assets API requests.
  • MICROGRID_CONFIG_DIR (optional): Directory containing TOML microgrid configs. Defaults to toml_directory/.
  • PARQUET_STORAGE_PATH (optional): Persistent directory for reporting data. Defaults to data/parquet.
  • SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES (optional): Minimum interval between overlap refreshes. Defaults to 15.
  • SYNC_OVERLAP_MINUTES (optional): Tail window re-fetched to pick up recent corrections. Defaults to 5.
  • API_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (optional): Reporting request timeout. Defaults to 300.

docs.title: Microgrid configs
docs.text: Microgrid definitions are loaded from TOML files in MICROGRID_CONFIG_DIR. The UI only lists configured microgrids returned by the Assets API for the current FREQUENZ_API_KEY and FREQUENZ_API_SECRET; inaccessible TOML entries are not displayed.

docs.title: Running the Streamlit app
docs.text:
The app entry point is app.py. When you run streamlit run app.py, it:

  • Discovers pages from frequenz.cs_reporting.app_pages (the default build ships Home and Reporting pages).
  • Loads microgrid configs from MICROGRID_CONFIG_DIR and lists available IDs.
  • Fetches data via the reporting API.

docs.title: Persistent data cache
docs.text:
Active-power, battery-SOC, and ENTSO-E day-ahead price time series are stored as Parquet. Microgrid measurements are separated by microgrid and resolution. The first request downloads the requested range; later requests read covered ranges locally and fetch only missing intervals. When a dataset is due for refresh, its trailing overlap is fetched again and merged by timestamp. Writes use a same-directory temporary file followed by an atomic replacement, while a file lock prevents duplicate writers across Streamlit sessions and local worker processes. Sync metadata is stored beside the Parquet directory in data/metadata by default. Runtime duration entries are appended to data/metadata/duration_log.txt; when PARQUET_STORAGE_PATH is customized, the log uses the sibling metadata directory of that configured path.

In Deepnote, the app automatically restores parquet and metadata from the persistent /work/data directory into the faster /tmp/frequenz-cs-reporting directory once per machine lifetime. Scheduled synchronization copies the updated local snapshot back to /work/data after a successful run. The Streamlit app also queues this copy in a background worker after rendering and after background dataset synchronization, so Parquet data, sync metadata, and duration logs survive machine restarts without delaying the page. Set DEEPNOTE_HYBRID_CACHE_ENABLED=false to disable this, or customize the roots with DEEPNOTE_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ROOT and DEEPNOTE_LOCAL_CACHE_ROOT.

Interactive reporting reads active-power data from the local cache and starts one shared background refresh when cached data is available. An empty cache is populated synchronously once so the initial load does not depend on browser timers in Deepnote; cached dashboards remain usable during later refreshes. Duration records are queued and written in batches by a background writer so diagnostic file I/O does not block Streamlit.

The reporting client used by this app exposes time-range queries, but not record modification timestamps, stable record IDs, change tokens, ETags, or a deletion feed. Consequently this is range-incremental synchronization, not a complete change-data-capture implementation. Corrections older than the overlap window require a wider explicit reconciliation request or rebuilding that dataset. Pagination remains owned by the upstream Frequenz clients. The cache retries transient connection, timeout, HTTP 429, and server errors with exponential backoff and honors Retry-After when the client exposes it.

For production, run synchronization independently from Streamlit, for example every 15 minutes with cron or the deployment platform's scheduler:

python -m frequenz.cs_reporting.services.sync_data \
  --microgrid-id 241 --lookback-days 30 --resolution-minutes 15

Synchronize the 15-minute day-ahead price dataset once per day after the new prices have been published (for example, after 14:00 local time):

python -m frequenz.cs_reporting.services.sync_data \
  --dataset day-ahead-prices --country-code DE_LU --lookback-days 30

When --end is omitted, the price job requests through the following day so the newly published prices remain available until the next scheduled run.

Streamlit reads day-ahead prices from this local cache without blocking the dashboard. If the requested range is missing, one shared in-process background job populates it while a small polling fragment waits. The dashboard initially renders without price-dependent content and reruns once when prices arrive. The daily scheduled job remains recommended so users normally receive an immediate cache hit.

Microgrid measurements remain a safe pull-through fallback: cache hits do not call the API, and failed overlap refreshes continue serving the last successful file. Point PARQUET_STORAGE_PATH at persistent storage. All replicas must see the same filesystem with working POSIX locks; ephemeral container disks and independent per-replica volumes do not provide a coherent shared cache. For those deployments, use a shared POSIX volume or replace this backend with object-storage/database coordination.

docs.title: Running in Deepnote
docs.text:
• Running in Deepnote is supported; required environment variables can be injected via the Deepnote integration.
  • Add this library as a requirement in requirements.txt
  • Add the docker image from dockerhub (currently named: CS-Reporting in deepnote).
  • Copy the app.py to the folder structure in Deepnote.
  • Click on create_streamlit_application in Deepnote UI to create the app.

docs.title: Library usage
docs.text:
Fetch microgrid data programmatically (sync wrapper shown):

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from frequenz.cs_reporting.services.data_service import get_microgrid_data

df = get_microgrid_data(
    microgrid_id=241,
    start_date=datetime(2024, 1, 1),
    end_date=datetime(2024, 1, 2),
    resolution=timedelta(minutes=15),
)

Build your own Streamlit page and add it to the navigation by defining a PageSpec in frequenz.cs_reporting.app_pages:

# app_pages/custom.py
from frequenz.cs_reporting.rep_cs_core.page_spec import PageSpec
import streamlit as st

def render() -> None:
    st.title("Custom view")
    st.write("Add your own charts or tables here.")

PAGE = PageSpec(key="custom", title="Custom", icon="🛠️", order=10, render=render)

python -m pip install build

docs.title: Local development
docs.text:
You can use editable installs to develop the project locally (it will install all the dependencies too):

python -m pip install -e .

Or you can install all development dependencies (mypy, pylint, pytest, etc.) in one go too: 

python -m pip install -e .[dev]

If you don't want to install all the dependencies, you can also use nox to run the tests and other checks creating its own virtual environments:

python -m pip install .[dev-noxfile]
nox

You can also use nox -R to reuse the current testing environment to speed up test at the expense of a higher chance to end up with a dirty test environment.

docs.title: Running tests / checks individually
docs.text:
For a better development test cycle you can install the runtime and test dependencies and run pytest manually.

python -m pip install .[dev-pytest]  # included in .[dev] too

# And for example
pytest tests/test_*.py

Or you can use nox:

nox -R -s pytest -- tests/test_*.py

The same applies to pylint or mypy for example:

nox -R -s pylint -- tests/test_*.py
nox -R -s mypy -- tests/test_*.py

docs.title: Building the documentation
docs.text:
To build the documentation, first install the dependencies (if you didn't install all dev dependencies):

python -m pip install -e .[dev-mkdocs]

Then you can build the documentation (it will be written in the site/ directory):

mkdocs build

Or you can just serve the documentation without building it using:

mkdocs serve

Your site will be updated live when you change your files (provided that you used pip install -e ., beware of a common pitfall of using pip install without -e, in that case the API reference won't change unless you do a new pip install).

To build multi-version documentation, we use mike. If you want to see how the multi-version sites looks like locally, you can use:

mike deploy my-version
mike set-default my-version
mike serve

mike works in mysterious ways. Some basic information:

  • mike deploy will do a mike build and write the results to your local gh-pages branch. my-version is an arbitrary name for the local version you want to preview.
  • mike set-default is needed so when you serve the documentation, it goes to your newly produced documentation by default.
  • mike serve will serve the contents of your local gh-pages branch. Be aware that, unlike mkdocs serve, changes to the sources won't be shown live, as the mike deploy step is needed to refresh them.

Be careful not to use --push with mike deploy, otherwise it will push your local gh-pages branch to the origin remote.

That said, if you want to test the actual website in your fork, you can always use mike deploy --push --remote your-fork-remote, and then access the GitHub pages produced for your fork.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
These are the steps to create a new release:

  1. Get the latest head you want to create a release from.

If you use milestones, check that the milestone for this release has no open issues left, and move whatever won't make it to a later milestone.

  1. Update the RELEASE_NOTES.md file if it is not complete, up to date, and remove template comments (<!-- ... -->) and empty sections. Submit a pull request if an update is needed, wait until it is merged, and update the latest head you want to create a release from to get the new merged pull request.

This can't be left for later: the notes published with the release are read from the RELEASE_NOTES.md committed at the tagged commit, not from the tag message.

  1. Create a new signed tag using the release notes and a semver compatible version number with a v prefix, for example:
git tag -s --cleanup=whitespace -F RELEASE_NOTES.md v0.0.1

The signature is not optional: the Protect released tags ruleset rejects unsigned tags. It also forbids updating or deleting a released tag, so make sure you are tagging the commit you want.

  1. Push the new tag.

  2. A GitHub action will test the tag and if all goes well it will create a GitHub Release, and upload a new package to PyPI automatically.

  3. Once this is done, reset the RELEASE_NOTES.md with the template:

cp .github/RELEASE_NOTES.template.md RELEASE_NOTES.md

Commit the new release notes and create a PR (this step should be automated eventually too).

  1. If you use milestones, close the milestone for this release, and create the next one if it doesn't exist yet.

  2. Celebrate!

def inject_style(style_name: str, **tokens: str) -> None:
    """Inject a packaged CSS stylesheet into the current Streamlit page.

    Tokens are replaced using ``__TOKEN_NAME__`` placeholders in the stylesheet.
    """
    style_text = load_style(style_name)
    for key, value in tokens.items():
        style_text = style_text.replace(f"__{key.upper()}__", value)

    st.markdown(f"<style>\n{style_text}\n</style>", unsafe_allow_html=True)

def render() -> None:
    """Render the Frequenz Reporting Dashboard page.

    Collects sidebar inputs, fetches microgrid data, prepares it for analysis,
    and renders the dashboard views.

    Returns:
        Streamlit components are rendered directly.
    """
    # Collect user inputs from sidebar
    today = datetime.now(tz=UTC).date()
    with log_duration("reporting.sidebar_inputs"):
        selections = collect_sidebar_inputs(
            default_start=today,
            default_end=today,
            resolution_options=("15min", "30min", "1hour"),
            default_resolution="15min",
            key_prefix="reporting_",
        )

    timezone = selections["timezone"]
    # Extract and convert inputs
    microgrid_id = selections["microgrid_id"]

    # set_date_to_midnight returns TZ-aware datetimes aligned with the user's timezone
    start_time = set_date_to_midnight(selections["start_date"], timezone)
    end_time = normalize_date_for_reporting(selections["end_date"], timezone)
    end_time = end_time.replace(microsecond=0)
    if end_time.date() != datetime.now(tz=UTC).date():
        end_time += timedelta(days=1)

    # Validate date range
    if start_time > end_time:
        st.warning(
            "Das Enddatum muss am oder nach dem Startdatum liegen. "
            "Bitte passen Sie Ihre Auswahl an."
        )
        st.stop()

    selected_period = end_time - start_time
    previous_start_time = start_time - selected_period

    try:
        resolution = _parse_resolution(selections["resolution"])
    except ValueError as exc:
        st.error(str(exc))
        st.stop()

    data_key = ReportingDataKey(
        microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
        start_iso=selections["start_date"].isoformat(),
        end_iso=selections["end_date"].isoformat(),
        timezone=timezone,
        resolution_seconds=int(resolution.total_seconds()),
    )

    # We extend the fetch end date by 1 day to ensure the API returns data
    # for the full duration of the selected end_time.

    # Fetch data with error handling
    active_power_sync: Future[pd.DataFrame] | None = None
    try:
        with st.spinner("Microgrid-Daten werden geladen..."):
            with log_duration("reporting.load_component_types"):
                component_types = list(get_component_types(microgrid_id))
            with log_duration("reporting.load_microgrid_config"):
                mcfg = get_microgrid_config(microgrid_id)
            with log_duration("reporting.load_microgrid_names"):
                microgrid_name = get_microgrid_names().get(microgrid_id) or mcfg.name
            heading = f"MID{microgrid_id}"
            if microgrid_name:
                heading = f"{heading} - {microgrid_name}"
            st.title(heading)
            snapshot = take_reporting_data_snapshot(data_key)
            if snapshot is not None:
                df = snapshot.active_power.copy()
                sync_metadata = snapshot.sync_metadata
                battery_soc_df = (
                    None
                    if snapshot.battery_soc is None
                    else snapshot.battery_soc.copy()
                )
            else:
                with log_duration("reporting.load_active_power"):
                    df, sync_metadata = get_cached_microgrid_data(
                        microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
                        start_date=previous_start_time,
                        end_date=end_time,
                        resolution=resolution,
                    )
                    if df.empty:
                        with log_duration("reporting.initial_active_power_sync"):
                            df = get_microgrid_data(
                                microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
                                start_date=previous_start_time,
                                end_date=end_time,
                                resolution=resolution,
                            )
                        sync_metadata = get_dataset_sync_metadata(
                            "active_power", microgrid_id, resolution
                        )
                    else:
                        active_power_sync = start_background_microgrid_data_sync(
                            microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
                            start_date=previous_start_time,
                            end_date=end_time,
                            resolution=resolution,
                        )
                battery_soc_df = None
            if sync_metadata.status == "error":
                last_sync = sync_metadata.last_successful_sync or "unbekannt"
                st.warning(
                    "Die Aktualisierung ist fehlgeschlagen; angezeigt werden die "
                    f"zuletzt erfolgreich gespeicherten Daten ({last_sync})."
                )
            battery_formula = (
                mcfg.ctype["battery"].formula if "battery" in component_types else None
            )
            has_battery_soc_formula = (
                battery_formula is not None and "BATTERY_SOC_PCT" in battery_formula
            )
            if snapshot is None and has_battery_soc_formula:
                try:
                    with log_duration("reporting.load_battery_soc"):
                        fetched_soc_df = get_cached_microgrid_soc_data(
                            microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
                            start_date=previous_start_time,
                            end_date=end_time,
                            resolution=resolution,
                        )
                        start_background_microgrid_soc_data_sync(
                            microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
                            start_date=previous_start_time,
                            end_date=end_time,
                            resolution=resolution,
                        )
                except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
                    st.warning(
                        f"Zwischengespeicherte Batterie-SOC-Daten konnten nicht "
                        f"geladen werden: {exc}"
                    )
                else:
                    battery_soc_df = None if fetched_soc_df.empty else fetched_soc_df
            if snapshot is None:
                store_reporting_data_snapshot(
                    ReportingDataSnapshot(
                        key=data_key,
                        active_power=df.copy(),
                        battery_soc=(
                            None if battery_soc_df is None else battery_soc_df.copy()
                        ),
                        sync_metadata=sync_metadata,
                    )
                )
    except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
        st.error(_format_data_loading_error(exc, microgrid_id))
        st.stop()

    # Check for empty results
    if df.empty:
        st.warning("Keine Daten für die ausgewählten Filter vorhanden.")
        st.stop()

    # Normalize the dataframe (Handle Index)
    with log_duration("reporting.prepare_dataframe"):
        df_prepared = _prepare_dataframe(df)

    # Build and render dashboard
    with log_duration("reporting.create_column_mapper"):
        mapper = ColumnMapper.from_default()
    with log_duration("reporting.build_master_dataframe"):
        master_df = build_master_df(
            df_prepared,
            component_types,
            mcfg,
            mapper,
            timezone=timezone,
            battery_soc_df=battery_soc_df,
        )
    with log_duration("reporting.split_periods"):
        current_master_df, previous_master_df = split_periods(
            master_df,
            start_time,
            end_time,
            resolution,
        )
    if current_master_df.empty:
        if active_power_sync is not None and not active_power_sync.done():
            _poll_active_power_sync(active_power_sync)
            st.stop()
        st.warning("Keine Daten für die ausgewählten Filter vorhanden.")
        st.stop()

    with log_duration("reporting.render_dashboard"):
        render_dashboard(
            current_master_df,
            resolution=resolution,
            component_types=component_types,
            mapper=mapper,
            microgrid_id=microgrid_id,
            mcfg=mcfg,
            previous_master_df=previous_master_df,
        )
    _scroll_to_section_if_requested()

@contextmanager
def capture_workflow_figures() -> Iterator[list[go.Figure]]:
    """Capture Plotly figures when the workflow attempts to display them.

    Yields:
        A list populated with Plotly figures while the workflow runs.
    """
    figures: list[go.Figure] = []

    def capture_figures(manager: plot_manager.PlotManager) -> None:
        figures.extend(
            figure
            for figure in manager.figures.values()
            if isinstance(figure, go.Figure) and figure.data
        )

    def suppress_notebook_display(_: object) -> None:
        return

    # frequenz-lib-notebooks keeps figures in local PlotManager instances and
    # renders them as a side effect. Capture the managers directly before the
    # figures reach IPython's display machinery.
    with _WORKFLOW_DISPLAY_LOCK:
        original_show_all = plot_manager.PlotManager.show_all
        original_table_display = getattr(plot_styles, "display")

                plot_data = asyncio.run(run_workflow(user_config_changes=user_request))

def plot_percentage_bar(
    data_points: dict[str, float | None], total_key: str
) -> go.Figure:
    """Render a stacked percentage bar showing contributions to a total.

    Args:
        data_points: Mapping of labels to numeric values.
        total_key: Key representing the total value in ``data_points``.

    Returns:
        Plotly figure containing the stacked bar chart.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``total_key`` is missing from ``data_points``.
    """
    if total_key not in data_points:
        raise ValueError(f"Total key '{total_key}' not found.")

    clean = {k: (float(v) if v is not None else 0.0) for k, v in data_points.items()}
    total = clean[total_key]

    if total <= 0:
        fig = go.Figure()
        fig.update_layout(
            paper_bgcolor="#ffffff",
            plot_bgcolor="#f8fafc",
            showlegend=False,
            annotations=[
                {
                    "text": "Keine Daten zur Anzeige",
                    "x": 0.5,
                    "xref": "paper",
                    "y": 0.5,
                    "yref": "paper",
                    "showarrow": False,
                    "font": {
                        "size": 13,
                        "color": "#94a3b8",
                        "family": "Inter, sans-serif",
                    },
                }
            ],
        )
        return fig

    segments = {
        k: v for k, v in clean.items() if k != total_key and isfinite(v) and v != 0.0
    }
    residual = total - sum(segments.values())
    if abs(residual) > 1e-6:
        segments["Sonstige"] = residual

    seg_with_pct = [
        (k, v, (v / total * 100.0 if total != 0 else 0.0)) for k, v in segments.items()
    ]
    seg_with_pct.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)

    # Assign palette colours in order; "Sonstige" always gets slate
    color_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    palette_idx = 0
    for label, _, _ in seg_with_pct:
        if label == "Sonstige":
            color_map[label] = _OTHERS_COLOR
        else:
            color_map[label] = _PROFESSIONAL_PALETTE[
                palette_idx % len(_PROFESSIONAL_PALETTE)
            ]
            palette_idx += 1

    fig = go.Figure()
    for label, value, pct in seg_with_pct:
        formatted_value = (
            f"{value:,.0f}".replace(",", "X").replace(".", ",").replace("X", ".")
        )
        fig.add_trace(
            go.Bar(
                x=[pct],
                y=[""],
                name=label,
                orientation="h",
                marker={
                    "color": color_map[label],
                    "line": {"color": "rgba(255,255,255,0.6)", "width": 1.5},
                },
                text=f"{pct:.1f}%",
                textposition="inside",
                insidetextanchor="middle",
                textfont={
                    "size": 11,
                    "color": "#ffffff",
                    "family": "Inter, sans-serif",
                },
                hovertext=[formatted_value],
                hovertemplate=(
                    f"<b>{label}</b><br>"
                    "Anteil: %{x:.1f}%<br>"
                    "Energie: %{hovertext} kWh"
                    "<extra></extra>"
                ),
            )
        )

    pos_total = sum(pct for _, _, pct in seg_with_pct if pct > 0)
    neg_total = sum(pct for _, _, pct in seg_with_pct if pct < 0)

    fig.update_layout(
        barmode="relative",
        font={"family": "Inter, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif", "size": 12},
        paper_bgcolor="#ffffff",
        plot_bgcolor="#f8fafc",
        xaxis={
            "title": None,
            "range": [min(0.0, neg_total * 1.1), max(100.0, pos_total * 1.05)],
            "tickformat": ".0f%%",
            "showgrid": False,
            "zeroline": False,
            "tickfont": {"size": 11, "color": "#9ca3af"},
        },
        yaxis={"showticklabels": False, "showgrid": False},
        height=150,
        margin={"l": 0, "r": 0, "t": 48, "b": 44},
        legend={
            "orientation": "h",
            "yanchor": "top",
            "y": -0.3,
            "xanchor": "center",
            "x": 0.5,
            "font": {"size": 11, "color": "#374151"},
            "bgcolor": "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
            "borderwidth": 0,
        },
        hoverlabel={
            "bgcolor": "#1e293b",
            "font_size": 12,
            "font_color": "#f8fafc",
            "bordercolor": "#334155",
        },
        separators=",.",
        annotations=[
            {
                "text": f"<b>{total_key}:</b> {total:,.0f}".replace(",", "X")
                .replace(".", ",")
                .replace("X", ".")
                + " kWh",
                "x": 0.5,
                "xref": "paper",
                "y": 1.35,
                "yref": "paper",
                "showarrow": False,
                "font": {
                    "size": 13,
                    "color": "#374151",
                    "family": "Inter, Segoe UI, Arial, sans-serif",
                },
            }
        ],
    )
    return fig

def collect_sidebar_inputs(
    *,
    default_start: date,
    default_end: date,
    resolution_options: Sequence[str] = ("15min", "30min", "1hour", "4hour"),
    default_resolution: str = "15min",
    timezone_options: Sequence[str] = TIMEZONE_OPTIONS,
    default_timezone: str = "Europe/Berlin",
    key_prefix: str = "",
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Render the sidebar filters.

    Creates an organized sidebar with sections for microgrid selection, date
    range, and resolution.

    Args:
        default_start: Default start date for the date picker.
        default_end: Default end date for the date picker.
        resolution_options: Allowed resolution values for selection.
        default_resolution: Default resolution shown initially.
        timezone_options: Allowed timezone values for selection.
        default_timezone: Default timezone shown initially.
        key_prefix: Optional prefix for Streamlit widget keys.

    Returns:
        Dictionary containing ``microgrid_id``, ``start_date``,
            ``end_date``, ``timezone``, and ``resolution`` selected by the user.
    """
    st.sidebar.header("Filter Einstellungen")
    st.sidebar.caption("Wählen Sie die Parameter für die Analyse.")

    form_key = f"{key_prefix}filters_form" if key_prefix else "filters_form"
    state_key = f"{key_prefix}applied_filters" if key_prefix else "applied_filters"

    with st.sidebar.form(form_key):
        st.subheader("Microgrid")
        microgrid_names = get_microgrid_names()
        microgrid_id = inputs.microgrid_selector(
            label="Microgrid-ID",
            ids=get_microgrid_ids(),
            format_func=lambda microgrid_id: _microgrid_option_label(
                microgrid_id, microgrid_names
            ),
            key_prefix=key_prefix,
            container=st,
        )

        st.divider()

        st.subheader("Zeitraum")

        today = datetime.now(tz=UTC).date()
        fallback_start = default_start or (today - timedelta(days=7))

        start_key = f"{key_prefix}start_date"
        end_key = f"{key_prefix}end_date"
        timezone_key = f"{key_prefix}timezone"

        start_initial = st.session_state.get(start_key, fallback_start)

        columns = st.columns(2)
        with columns[0]:
            start_date = st.date_input(
                "Von",
                value=start_initial,
                max_value=today,
                key=start_key,
            )

        end_initial = min(
            st.session_state.get(end_key, default_end or today),
            today,
        )

        with columns[1]:
            end_date = st.date_input(
                "Ende",
                value=end_initial,
                max_value=today,
                key=end_key,
            )

        timezone_options_list = list(timezone_options)
        timezone_index = next(
            (
                idx
                for idx, option in enumerate(timezone_options_list)
                if option == default_timezone
            ),
            0,
        )

        timezone = st.selectbox(
            "Zeitzone",
            options=timezone_options_list,
            index=timezone_index,
            key=timezone_key,
            help="Zeitzone zur Interpretation der ausgewählten Tage",
        )

        st.divider()

        resolution = st.selectbox(
            "Auflösung",
            options=list(resolution_options),
            index=next(
                (
                    idx
                    for idx, option in enumerate(resolution_options)
                    if option == default_resolution
                ),
                0,
            ),
            key=f"{key_prefix}resolution",
            help="Zeitliche Auflösung der Daten",
        )

        st.divider()

        submitted = st.form_submit_button(
            "Filter anwenden", use_container_width=True, type="primary"
        )

    current_selection = {
        "microgrid_id": microgrid_id,
        "start_date": start_date,
        "end_date": end_date,
        "timezone": timezone,
        "resolution": resolution,
    }

    if submitted or state_key not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[state_key] = current_selection

    return dict(st.session_state[state_key])

def collect_solar_sidebar_inputs(
    *,
    default_start_date: date,

    default_baseline_models: Sequence[str] | None = None,

    df: pd.DataFrame,
    *,
    key_prefix: str,
    page_size: int = 7,
    header_color: str = "#1e4f87",
    height: int | None = None,
    theme: str = "balham",  # 'alpine' | 'balham' | 'material' | etc.
    default_col_width: int = 180,
    min_col_width: int = 160,
    download_file_name: str | None = None,
    component_source: str | None = None,
) -> str | None:
    """Render a dataframe using AgGrid with sensible defaults.

    Args:
        df: Dataframe to display; an empty dataframe is used when invalid.
        key_prefix: Unique prefix for Streamlit state keys.
        page_size: Preferred page size for pagination controls.
        header_color: Header background color.
        height: Height of the grid container in pixels.
        theme: AgGrid theme name.
        default_col_width: Default column width in pixels.
        min_col_width: Minimum column width in pixels.
        download_file_name: Optional CSV filename. When provided, a download
            button is rendered beside the filter-reset button.
        component_source: Selected component source. When provided, its selector
            is rendered before the reset and download buttons.

    Returns:
        The selected component source when its selector is enabled, otherwise
        ``None``.
    """
    if df is None or not isinstance(df, pd.DataFrame):
        df = pd.DataFrame()

    if f"{key_prefix}_page_size" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[f"{key_prefix}_page_size"] = page_size

        if isinstance(selected_source, str):

    return None

def render_plot_card(
    title: str,
    fig: object,
    header_control: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
    key: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Render a plot inside a styled card.

    Args:
        title: Title displayed in the card header.
        fig: Plotly or Matplotlib figure to render.
        header_control: Optional Streamlit control rendered at the right side of
            the card header.
        key: Optional key used to style cards that include header controls.

    Returns:
        Streamlit components are rendered directly.
    """
    _ensure_plot_card_css()
    card_key = f"{key or title.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_plot_card"
    header_key = f"{key or title.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_plot_header"

    if header_control is not None:
        with st.container(key=card_key, height=_plot_card_height(fig)):
            with st.container(
                key=header_key,
                horizontal=True,
                vertical_alignment="center",
                horizontal_alignment="distribute",
            ):
                st.markdown(
                    f"""
                    <div class="plot-card__native-title-wrap">
                        <div class="plot-card__header-dot"></div>
                        <p class="plot-card__title">{title}</p>
                    </div>
                    """,
                    unsafe_allow_html=True,
                )
                header_control()

            if isinstance(fig, go.Figure):
                st.plotly_chart(
                    fig,
                    width="stretch",
                    height=_plotly_component_height(fig),
                )
            elif isinstance(fig, Figure):
                st.pyplot(fig)
            else:
                st.warning("Nicht unterstützter Figurtyp.")
        return

    with st.container(key=card_key, height=_plot_card_height(fig)):
        st.markdown(
            f"""
            <div class="plot-card__header">
                <div class="plot-card__header-dot"></div>
                <p class="plot-card__title">{title}</p>
            </div>
            """,
            unsafe_allow_html=True,
        )

        if isinstance(fig, go.Figure):
            st.plotly_chart(
                fig,
                width="stretch",
                height=_plotly_component_height(fig),
            )
        elif isinstance(fig, Figure):
            st.pyplot(fig)
        else:
            st.warning("Nicht unterstützter Figurtyp.")

@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_meter_display_names(microgrid_id: int) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return component display names for a microgrid from the Assets API.

    Args:
        microgrid_id: Identifier for the target microgrid.

    Returns:
        Mapping of component ID strings to display names.
    """
    auth_key = require_env("FREQUENZ_API_KEY")
    sign_secret = require_env("FREQUENZ_API_SECRET")
    assets_api_url = require_env("ASSETS_API_URL")

    async def load() -> dict[str, str]:
        assets_client = AssetsApiClient(
            assets_api_url,
            auth_key=auth_key,
            sign_secret=sign_secret,
        )
        try:
            components = await assets_client.list_microgrid_electrical_components(
                MicrogridId(microgrid_id)
            )
            return {
                str(component.id): component.name
                for component in components
                if component.name
            }
        finally:
            await assets_client.disconnect()

    return asyncio.run(load())

def get_microgrid_data(
    microgrid_id: int,
    start_date: datetime,
    end_date: datetime,
    resolution: timedelta,
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load active-power data through the persistent Parquet cache.

    Args:
        microgrid_id: Identifier for the target microgrid.
        start_date: Inclusive start date of the query range.
        end_date: Exclusive end date of the query range.
        resolution: Resampling period for the returned data.
        timeout: Request timeout in seconds. Uses configuration when omitted.

    Returns:
        Dataframe of AC active power measurements. Empty when no
            data is available.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If invoked from within an active event loop instead of
            using the async ``fetch_microgrid_data``.
    """
    try:
        asyncio.get_running_loop()
    except RuntimeError:
        # No active loop: safe to block
        config = get_cache_config()
        effective_timeout = timeout or float(config.request_timeout_seconds)
        cache = ParquetRangeCache(
            config.storage_path,
            sync_interval=timedelta(minutes=config.sync_interval_minutes),
            overlap=timedelta(minutes=config.sync_overlap_minutes),
        )
        with log_duration("data.active_power.cache_get"):
            return cache.get(
                _dataset_key("active_power", microgrid_id, resolution),
                start_date,
                end_date,
                lambda fetch_start, fetch_end: asyncio.run(
                    fetch_microgrid_data(
                        microgrid_id,
                        fetch_start,
                        fetch_end,
                        resolution,
                        timeout=effective_timeout,
                    )
                ),
            )
    # Active loop: force caller to use the async API
    raise RuntimeError(
        "get_microgrid_data() called from within an active event loop. "
        "Use `await fetch_microgrid_data(...)` in async contexts."
    )

def start_background_day_ahead_price_sync(
    country_code: str,
    start_date: datetime,
    end_date: datetime,
) -> Future[pd.Series]:
    """Start one non-blocking price synchronization for a normalized date range.

    Concurrent Streamlit sessions share the same in-process job. Failed or
    empty synchronizations are held for a short cooldown to avoid retry loops
    on every rerun.

    Args:
        country_code: ENTSO-E bidding-zone country code.
        start_date: Inclusive beginning of the required price range.
        end_date: Exclusive end of the required price range.

    Returns:
        Future representing the background synchronization.
    """
    sync_start, sync_end = _day_ahead_sync_range(start_date, end_date)
    key = (country_code, sync_start, sync_end)
    now = monotonic()
    with _DAY_AHEAD_SYNC_LOCK:
        existing = _DAY_AHEAD_SYNC_JOBS.get(key)
        if existing is not None:
            future, started = existing
            if not future.done() or now - started < _DAY_AHEAD_SYNC_RETRY_INTERVAL:
                return future

        future = _DAY_AHEAD_SYNC_EXECUTOR.submit(
            get_day_ahead_prices,
            country_code,
            sync_start,
            sync_end,
        )
        future.add_done_callback(_persist_cache_after_successful_sync)
        _DAY_AHEAD_SYNC_JOBS[key] = (future, now)
        return future

def persist_deepnote_hybrid_cache(
    persistent_root: Path | None = None,
    local_root: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Copy the fast local cache back to Deepnote's persistent storage.

    This should be called after a scheduled synchronization rather than only
    at process shutdown, which is not guaranteed to run in Deepnote.

    Args:
        persistent_root: Durable cache root, defaulting to ``/work/data``.
        local_root: Fast ephemeral cache root, defaulting to
            ``/tmp/frequenz-cs-reporting``.
    """
    # Timing writes are already asynchronous, so waiting here only blocks this
    # persistence worker (or an explicit scheduled command), never Streamlit.
    # It ensures duration_log.txt is part of the same persistent snapshot.
    flush_timing_log()
    persistent = persistent_root or Path(
        os.getenv("DEEPNOTE_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ROOT", str(_DEFAULT_PERSISTENT_ROOT))
    )
    local = local_root or Path(
        os.getenv("DEEPNOTE_LOCAL_CACHE_ROOT", str(_DEFAULT_LOCAL_ROOT))
    )
    persistent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for directory in _CACHE_DIRECTORIES:
        source = local / directory
        if source.is_dir():
            destination = persistent / directory
            shutil.copytree(source, destination, dirs_exist_ok=True)
            _fsync_files(destination)

        os.getenv("DEEPNOTE_PERSISTENT_CACHE_ROOT", str(_DEFAULT_PERSISTENT_ROOT))
    )
    local = local_root or Path(
        os.getenv("DEEPNOTE_LOCAL_CACHE_ROOT", str(_DEFAULT_LOCAL_ROOT))
    )
    # Create the durable layout up front.  Besides making the configured
    # storage visible immediately in Deepnote, this validates that the project
    # mount is writable before a scheduled synchronization needs it.
    for directory in _CACHE_DIRECTORIES:
        (persistent / directory).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    local.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    marker = local / _INITIALIZED_MARKER
    if not marker.exists():
        for directory in _CACHE_DIRECTORIES:
            source = persistent / directory
            destination = local / directory
            if source.is_dir():
                shutil.copytree(source, destination, dirs_exist_ok=True)
            else:
                destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        marker.touch()

    parquet_path = local / "parquet"
    parquet_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (local / "metadata").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ["PARQUET_STORAGE_PATH"] = str(parquet_path)
    return parquet_path

def start_background_deepnote_cache_persist() -> Future[None] | None:
    """Persist the local Deepnote cache without blocking Streamlit.

    Multiple requests are coalesced.  If another request arrives while a copy
    is running, the worker performs one additional pass so updates created
    during the first copy cannot be missed.

    Returns:
        The active persistence future, or ``None`` outside an enabled Deepnote
        hybrid-cache environment.
    """
    global _PERSIST_FUTURE, _PERSIST_PENDING  # pylint: disable=global-statement

    if not running_in_deepnote() or not deepnote_hybrid_cache_enabled():
        return None

    with _PERSIST_LOCK:
        if _PERSIST_FUTURE is not None and not _PERSIST_FUTURE.done():
            _PERSIST_PENDING = True
            return _PERSIST_FUTURE
        _PERSIST_PENDING = False
        _PERSIST_FUTURE = _PERSIST_EXECUTOR.submit(_persist_until_idle)
        return _PERSIST_FUTURE

class ParquetRangeCache:
    """Synchronize API time ranges into an atomic local Parquet dataset."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        root: Path,
        *,
        sync_interval: timedelta,
        overlap: timedelta,
        retry_attempts: int = 3,
        sleeper: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a cache rooted at the configured Parquet directory."""
        self._root = root
        self._metadata_root = root.parent / "metadata"
        self._sync_interval = sync_interval
        self._overlap = overlap
        self._retry_attempts = retry_attempts
        self._sleeper = sleeper

    # pylint: disable = too-many-locals
    def get(
        self,
        key: DatasetKey,
        start: datetime,
        end: datetime,
        fetch: Callable[[datetime, datetime], pd.DataFrame],
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return a requested range, synchronizing missing or stale data."""
        requested = (_utc(start), _utc(end))
        if requested[0] >= requested[1]:
            raise ValueError("The cache range end must be after its start")

        self._root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._metadata_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._lock(key):
            metadata = self._read_metadata(key)
            stored, storage_valid = self._read_frame(key)
            covered = self._metadata_ranges(metadata)
            if not storage_valid:
                covered = []
            required = _subtract_range(requested, covered)
            now = datetime.now(tz=UTC)
            due = _sync_due(metadata.last_successful_sync, now, self._sync_interval)
            if not due and _is_small_trailing_extension(
                required, covered, self._sync_interval
            ):
                required = []

            ranges = list(required)
            if due and covered:
                watermark = max(range_end for _, range_end in covered)
                coverage_start = min(range_start for range_start, _ in covered)
                refresh_start = max(coverage_start, watermark - self._overlap)
                if refresh_start < watermark:
                    ranges.append((refresh_start, watermark))
            ranges = _merge_ranges(ranges)

            if ranges:
                stored, metadata = self._synchronize(
                    key, stored, metadata, covered, ranges, fetch, now
                )

            return _slice_frame(stored, requested, metadata)

    def read(
        self,
        key: DatasetKey,
        start: datetime,
        end: datetime,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return cached data without synchronizing missing or stale ranges.

        Args:
            key: Dataset identifier.
            start: Inclusive start of the requested range.
            end: Exclusive end of the requested range.

        Returns:
            The locally cached slice, or an empty dataframe when no valid cache
            exists.  This method never calls an external data source.
        """
        frame, _ = self.read_with_metadata(key, start, end)
        return frame

    def read_with_metadata(
        self,
        key: DatasetKey,
        start: datetime,
        end: datetime,
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, SyncMetadata]:
        """Return a cached range and the metadata read for that same operation."""
        requested = (_utc(start), _utc(end))
        if requested[0] >= requested[1]:
            raise ValueError("The cache range end must be after its start")

        self._root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._metadata_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        metadata = self._read_metadata(key)
        stored, storage_valid = self._read_frame(key)
        if not storage_valid:
            return pd.DataFrame(), metadata
        return _slice_frame(stored, requested, metadata), metadata

    def metadata(self, key: DatasetKey) -> SyncMetadata:
        """Read synchronization metadata for status display or monitoring."""
        return self._read_metadata(key)

    # pylint: disable = too-many-locals, too-many-arguments, too-many-positional-arguments
    def _synchronize(
        self,
        key: DatasetKey,
        stored: pd.DataFrame,
        metadata: SyncMetadata,
        covered: list[_Range],
        ranges: list[_Range],
        fetch: Callable[[datetime, datetime], pd.DataFrame],
        attempted_at: datetime,
    ) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, SyncMetadata]:
        started = time.monotonic()
        metadata.last_attempted_sync = _iso(attempted_at)
        metadata.status = "syncing"
        metadata.last_error = None

        try:
            raw_parts: list[tuple[pd.DataFrame, datetime, datetime]] = []
            incoming_axis: tuple[str, str | None] | None = None
            for range_start, range_end in ranges:
                raw_frame = self._fetch_with_retry(fetch, range_start, range_end)
                if not raw_frame.empty and incoming_axis is None:
                    incoming_axis = _raw_frame_axis(raw_frame)
                raw_parts.append((raw_frame, range_start, range_end))

            with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "normalize")):
                incoming_parts = [
                    _normalize_frame(
                        raw_frame,
                        range_start,
                        range_end,
                        tolerance=timedelta(seconds=key.resolution_seconds),
                    )
                    for raw_frame, range_start, range_end in raw_parts
                ]
                incoming = _concat_frames(incoming_parts)
                normalized_stored = _normalize_stored(stored)

            with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "merge")):
                merged = _merge_frames(normalized_stored, incoming)
                axis, index_name = incoming_axis or (
                    metadata.timestamp_axis,
                    metadata.index_name,
                )
                new_covered = _merge_ranges([*covered, *ranges])

            self._write_frame(key, merged)
            metadata.covered_ranges = [
                [_iso(range_start), _iso(range_end)]
                for range_start, range_end in new_covered
            ]
            metadata.timestamp_axis = axis
            metadata.index_name = index_name
            metadata.last_successful_sync = _iso(attempted_at)
            metadata.status = "ok"
            metadata.records_retrieved = len(incoming)
            metadata.records_inserted_or_updated = len(incoming)
            metadata.total_stored_records = len(merged)
            metadata.sync_duration_seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
            metadata.last_error = None
            self._write_metadata(key, metadata)
            return merged, metadata
        except Exception as exc:
            metadata.status = "error"
            metadata.sync_duration_seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
            metadata.last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
            self._write_metadata(key, metadata)
            _LOGGER.exception("Synchronization failed for %s", key.slug)
            if _range_is_covered(ranges, covered):
                return stored, metadata
            raise

    def _fetch_with_retry(
        self,
        fetch: Callable[[datetime, datetime], pd.DataFrame],
        start: datetime,
        end: datetime,
    ) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Retry transient transport and server failures with backoff."""
        for attempt in range(self._retry_attempts):
            try:
                return fetch(start, end)
            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
                if attempt + 1 >= self._retry_attempts or not _is_transient(exc):
                    raise
                delay = _retry_after_seconds(exc) or (0.5 * (2**attempt))
                _LOGGER.warning(
                    "Transient sync failure; retrying %s in %.1f seconds",
                    type(exc).__name__,
                    delay,
                )
                self._sleeper(delay)
        raise AssertionError("retry loop exited unexpectedly")

    def _read_frame(self, key: DatasetKey) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, bool]:
        with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "read_parquet")):
            path = self._data_path(key)
            if not path.exists():
                return pd.DataFrame(), False
            version = (path.stat().st_mtime_ns, path.stat().st_size)
            try:
                return _read_parquet_versioned(str(path), version), True
            except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
                _LOGGER.exception("Ignoring unreadable Parquet cache %s", path)
                return pd.DataFrame(), False

    def _write_frame(self, key: DatasetKey, frame: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
        with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "write_parquet")):
            path = self._data_path(key)
            temporary = _temporary_path(path, ".parquet.tmp")
            try:
                encoded = frame.copy()
                encoded.columns = [_encode_column(column) for column in frame.columns]
                encoded.to_parquet(temporary, engine="pyarrow", index=True)
                os.replace(temporary, path)
            finally:
                temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def _read_metadata(self, key: DatasetKey) -> SyncMetadata:
        with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "read_metadata")):
            path = self._metadata_path(key)
            if not path.exists():
                return SyncMetadata(dataset=key.slug)
            try:
                values = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                if not isinstance(values, dict):
                    raise ValueError("metadata root must be an object")
                metadata = SyncMetadata.from_dict(values)
                # Versions before the boundary-filtering fix recorded valid API
                # responses as failures. Do not keep presenting that obsolete
                # false-positive after an application restart.
                if metadata.last_error == _LEGACY_BOUNDARY_ERROR:
                    metadata.status = "ok"
                    metadata.last_error = None
                return metadata
            except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
                _LOGGER.exception("Ignoring invalid cache metadata %s", path)
                return SyncMetadata(dataset=key.slug)

    def _write_metadata(self, key: DatasetKey, metadata: SyncMetadata) -> None:
        with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "write_metadata")):
            path = self._metadata_path(key)
            temporary = _temporary_path(path, ".json.tmp")
            try:
                with temporary.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as output:
                    json.dump(asdict(metadata), output, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
                    output.flush()
                    if not _is_ephemeral_path(path):
                        os.fsync(output.fileno())
                os.replace(temporary, path)
            finally:
                temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    @contextmanager
    def _lock(self, key: DatasetKey) -> Iterator[None]:
        lock_path = self._metadata_root / f"{key.slug}.lock"
        with lock_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as lock_file:
            with log_duration(_cache_timing_operation(key, "lock_wait")):
                fcntl.flock(lock_file.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                fcntl.flock(lock_file.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

    def _data_path(self, key: DatasetKey) -> Path:
        return self._root / f"{key.slug}.parquet"

    def _metadata_path(self, key: DatasetKey) -> Path:
        return self._metadata_root / f"{key.slug}.json"

    def _metadata_ranges(self, metadata: SyncMetadata) -> list[_Range]:
        try:
            return _merge_ranges(
                [(_parse(start), _parse(end)) for start, end in metadata.covered_ranges]
            )
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            _LOGGER.warning("Discarding invalid ranges for %s", metadata.dataset)
            return []

def build_workflow_request(
    *,
    microgrid_id: int,
    config: MicrogridConfig,
    start_date: datetime.date,
    time_zone: str,
    component_category: str,
    language: str,
    resample_period: str,
    rolling_view_duration: int,
    baseline_models: list[str],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the request payload for triggering the solar workflow.

    Assembles all required parameters into a dictionary suitable for submitting
    a solar workflow request. This includes time boundaries, localization settings,
    component selection, site metadata, baseline configuration, and service
    endpoints derived from the environment.

    Args:
        microgrid_id:
            Identifier of the microgrid for which the workflow is executed.
        config:
            Microgrid configuration used to resolve component IDs and site metadata.
        start_date:
            Start date of the analysis period. The timestamp is normalized to
            midnight UTC.
        time_zone:
            Time zone identifier used by the workflow for localization.
        component_category:
            Component category used to filter PV component IDs.
        language:
            Human-readable language selection (e.g., "English", "Deutsch").
        resample_period:
            Large resampling period in seconds, provided as a string.
        rolling_view_duration:
            Requested rolling view duration in days. The effective duration is
            capped by the number of days since `start_date`.
        baseline_models:
            List of baseline model identifiers to be applied by the workflow.

    Returns:
            A dictionary representing the complete workflow request payload,
            including timestamps, localization options, component IDs, site
            metadata, service endpoints, and model configuration.
    """
    start_dt = datetime.datetime.combine(
        start_date, datetime.time.min, tzinfo=datetime.UTC
    )
    end_timestamp = datetime.datetime.now(tz=datetime.UTC)

    days_since_start = max(0, (end_timestamp - start_dt).days)
    actual_rolling_duration = min(rolling_view_duration, days_since_start)
    lang_code = {"English": "en", "Englisch": "en", "Deutsch": "de"}.get(language, "de")

    weather_api = os.environ.get("WEATHER_API_URL")
    reporting_api = os.environ.get("REPORTING_API_URL")

    return {
        "time_zone": time_zone,
        "start_timestamp": start_dt,
        "end_timestamp": end_timestamp,
        "rolling_view_duration": actual_rolling_duration,
        "language": lang_code,
        "weather_service_address": weather_api,
        "reporting_service_address": reporting_api,
        "microgrid_ids": [microgrid_id],
        "component_ids": [
            config.component_type_ids(
                component_type="pv", component_category=component_category
            )
        ],
        "client_site_info": [_build_client_site_info(config)],
        "baseline_models": baseline_models,
        "large_resample_period_seconds": int(resample_period),

def main() -> None:
    """Synchronize configured datasets for use by cron or a platform scheduler."""
    use_hybrid_cache = deepnote_hybrid_cache_enabled() and any(
        key in os.environ
        for key in ("DEEPNOTE_PROJECT_ID", "DEEPNOTE_WORKSPACE_ID", "DEEPNOTE")
    )
    if use_hybrid_cache:
        prepare_deepnote_hybrid_cache()

    parser = _parser()
    args = parser.parse_args()
    end = args.end or datetime.now(tz=UTC)
    start = args.start or end - timedelta(days=args.lookback_days)
    resolution = timedelta(minutes=args.resolution_minutes)
    if start >= end:
        raise SystemExit("--start must be earlier than --end")
    if resolution <= timedelta(0):
        raise SystemExit("--resolution-minutes must be greater than zero")
    if args.dataset != "day-ahead-prices" and not args.microgrid_id:
        parser.error("--microgrid-id is required for the selected dataset")

    for microgrid_id in args.microgrid_id or []:
        if args.dataset in ("active-power", "all"):
            get_microgrid_data(microgrid_id, start, end, resolution)
        if args.dataset in ("battery-soc", "all"):
            get_microgrid_soc_data(microgrid_id, start, end, resolution)
    if args.dataset in ("day-ahead-prices", "all"):
        # The afternoon publication contains future prices. Keep tomorrow's
        # values so the dashboard remains covered until the next daily run.
        price_end = args.end or end + timedelta(days=1)
        get_day_ahead_prices(args.country_code, start, price_end)
    if use_hybrid_cache:
        persist_deepnote_hybrid_cache()

    """Validate that the start value precedes the end value.

    Args:
        start: Start date or datetime value.
        end: End date or datetime value.

    Returns:
        Original ``start`` and ``end`` values when valid.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``start`` is greater than or equal to ``end``.
    """
    start_ts = to_datetime(start)
    end_ts = to_datetime(end)

    if start_ts.tzinfo is None:
        start_ts = start_ts.tz_localize(UTC)
    else:
        start_ts = start_ts.tz_convert(UTC)

    if end_ts.tzinfo is None:
        end_ts = end_ts.tz_localize(UTC)
    else:
        end_ts = end_ts.tz_convert(UTC)

    start_dt = start_ts.to_pydatetime()
    end_dt = end_ts.to_pydatetime()
    if end_dt <= start_dt:
        raise ValueError("end_date must be after start_date")
    return start_dt, end_dt

    mcfg: Any,

    1. Overview section with summary metric boxes
    2. Interactive plots section with time series and pie charts
    3. Data tables section with detailed component breakdowns

def split_periods(
    master_df: pd.DataFrame,
    start_time: datetime,
    end_time: datetime,
    resolution: timedelta,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Split a fetched master dataframe into selected and previous periods."""
    if master_df.empty:
        return master_df.copy(), master_df.copy()

    period = end_time - start_time
    previous_start = start_time - period

    timestamps = _timestamp_series_utc(master_df)
    selected_start = _timestamp_utc(start_time)
    selected_end = _timestamp_utc(end_time)
    previous_start_ts = _timestamp_utc(previous_start)

    current_mask = (timestamps >= selected_start) & (timestamps < selected_end)
    current_timestamps = timestamps.loc[current_mask]
    if current_timestamps.empty:
        return master_df.loc[current_mask].copy(), master_df.loc[current_mask].copy()

    actual_selected_end = min(
        selected_end,
        current_timestamps.max() + pd.Timedelta(resolution),
    )
    previous_end_ts = previous_start_ts + (actual_selected_end - selected_start)
    previous_mask = (timestamps >= previous_start_ts) & (timestamps < previous_end_ts)

    return master_df.loc[current_mask].copy(), master_df.loc[previous_mask].copy()

    master_df: pd.DataFrame,
    tables_dict: TablesResult,
    mapper: ColumnMapper,
    mcfg: Any,
    component_types: Iterable[str],
) -> None:
    """Render tabbed data tables for overview and component analyses.

    Args:
        master_df: Processed master dataframe.
        tables_dict: Mapping of table names to dataframes for each analysis.
        mapper: Column mapper for standardizing Gesamt-Datensatz column names.
        mcfg: Microgrid configuration object containing component metadata.
        component_types: Component type identifiers present in the microgrid.

    Returns:
        Streamlit components are rendered directly.
    """
    available_specs = []
    for spec in TABLE_TAB_SPECS:
        if _table_spec_has_data(spec, tables_dict, master_df, mcfg, component_types):
            available_specs.append(spec)

    include_master = master_df is not None and not master_df.empty

    if not available_specs and not include_master:
        st.info("Keine Datentabellen verfügbar.")
        return

    tab_labels: list[str] = []
    if include_master:
        tab_labels.extend(("Kerndaten", "Gesamt-Datensatz"))
    tab_labels.extend(spec["label"] for spec in available_specs)
    tabs = st.tabs(tab_labels)

    table_tabs = tabs
    if include_master:
        with tabs[0]:
            render_core_data(master_df)
        with tabs[1]:
            render_master_df(master_df, mapper)
        table_tabs = tabs[2:]

    for tab, spec in zip(table_tabs, available_specs):
        value = tables_dict.get(spec["table_key"])
        with tab:
            analysis_key = spec.get("analysis_key")
            empty_info = spec.get("empty_info")
            if analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS:
                table_key = str(spec["table_key"])

                selected_source = selected_component_plot_source(
                    mcfg,

                    analysis_key,
                    state_key=f"{table_key}_component_plot_source",
                    source_has_data=_component_source_has_data_callback(

                    )

                    if analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS

    if not metrics:

        return

    _ensure_kpi_css()
    component_types_provided = component_types is not None
    component_type_set = set(component_types or [])

def render_workflow_results(plot_data: Any, figures: list[go.Figure]) -> None:
    """Render and display results returned by the solar workflow.

    Handles multiple possible result types produced by the workflow and renders
    them appropriately in the Streamlit UI. Supported outputs include structured
    analysis objects, dictionaries, lists of figures or tables, Plotly figures,
    and generic displayable values. Plotly figures emitted during the workflow
    are displayed in a dedicated section.

    Args:
        plot_data:
            Result object returned by the workflow. This may be a
            ``SolarAnalysisData`` instance, a dictionary, a list of renderable
            objects, a Plotly figure, or a generic displayable value.
        figures:
            Plotly figures collected from the workflow's plot managers.

    Returns:
        None. All outputs are rendered directly in the Streamlit UI.
    """
    if not plot_data:
        st.warning("Vom Workflow wurden keine Daten zurückgegeben.")
        return

    if isinstance(plot_data, SolarAnalysisData):
        _render_production_table(plot_data)

    elif isinstance(plot_data, dict):
        for key, value in plot_data.items():
            st.subheader(key)
            if isinstance(value, go.Figure):
                render_plot_card(str(key), value)
            else:
                st.write(value)

    elif isinstance(plot_data, list):
        for idx, item in enumerate(plot_data, start=1):
            if isinstance(item, go.Figure):
                render_plot_card(_plot_title(item, f"Diagramm {idx}"), item)
            else:
                st.write(item)
    elif isinstance(plot_data, go.Figure):
        render_plot_card(_plot_title(plot_data, "Solar-Diagramm"), plot_data)
    else:
        st.write(plot_data)

    populated_figures = [figure for figure in figures if figure.data]
    if populated_figures:
        st.divider()
        st.markdown("#### Workflow-Abbildungen")

        for idx, fig in enumerate(populated_figures, start=1):
            render_plot_card(_plot_title(fig, f"Abbildung {idx}"), fig)
    elif isinstance(plot_data, SolarAnalysisData):
        st.warning("Der Workflow hat keine darstellbaren Diagramme erzeugt.")

def render_data_tabs(
    master_df: pd.DataFrame,
    tables_dict: TablesResult,
    mapper: ColumnMapper,
    mcfg: Any,
    component_types: Iterable[str],
) -> None:
    """Render tabbed data tables for overview and component analyses.

    Args:
        master_df: Processed master dataframe.
        tables_dict: Mapping of table names to dataframes for each analysis.
        mapper: Column mapper for standardizing Gesamt-Datensatz column names.
        mcfg: Microgrid configuration object containing component metadata.
        component_types: Component type identifiers present in the microgrid.

    Returns:
        Streamlit components are rendered directly.
    """
    available_specs = []
    for spec in TABLE_TAB_SPECS:
        if _table_spec_has_data(spec, tables_dict, master_df, mcfg, component_types):
            available_specs.append(spec)

    include_master = master_df is not None and not master_df.empty

    if not available_specs and not include_master:
        st.info("Keine Datentabellen verfügbar.")
        return

    tab_labels: list[str] = []
    if include_master:
        tab_labels.extend(("Kerndaten", "Gesamt-Datensatz"))
    tab_labels.extend(spec["label"] for spec in available_specs)
    tabs = st.tabs(tab_labels)

    table_tabs = tabs
    if include_master:
        with tabs[0]:
            render_core_data(master_df)
        with tabs[1]:
            render_master_df(master_df, mapper)
        table_tabs = tabs[2:]

    for tab, spec in zip(table_tabs, available_specs):
        value = tables_dict.get(spec["table_key"])
        with tab:
            analysis_key = spec.get("analysis_key")
            empty_info = spec.get("empty_info")
            if analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS:
                table_key = str(spec["table_key"])
                analysis_key = str(analysis_key)
                selected_source = selected_component_plot_source(
                    mcfg,
                    component_types,
                    analysis_key,
                    state_key=f"{table_key}_component_plot_source",
                    source_has_data=_component_source_has_data_callback(
                        master_df,
                        mcfg,
                        component_types,
                        analysis_key,
                    ),
                )
                value = _component_analysis_table_for_source(
                    master_df,
                    mcfg,
                    component_types,
                    analysis_key,
                    selected_source,
                )

            render_table_section(
                value if isinstance(value, pd.DataFrame) else None,
                key_prefix=spec["key_prefix"],
                empty_info=(
                    None
                    if (
                        analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS
                        and selected_source == "meter"
                        and (not isinstance(value, pd.DataFrame) or value.empty)
                    )
                    else empty_info
                ),
                component_source=(
                    selected_source
                    if analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS
                    else None
                ),
                component_source_state_key=(
                    f"{table_key}_component_plot_source"
                    if analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS
                    else None
                ),
            )
            if (
                analysis_key in PLOT_SOURCE_ANALYSIS_KEYS
                and selected_source == "meter"
                and (not isinstance(value, pd.DataFrame) or value.empty)
            ):
                st.warning("Meter-Daten sind nicht verfügbar.")

def render_table_section(
    df: pd.DataFrame | None,
    *,
    key_prefix: str,
    empty_info: str | None = None,
    component_source: str | None = None,
    component_source_state_key: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Render a captioned AgGrid table, safely handling None/empty data.

    Args:
        df: The dataframe to display. If ``None`` or empty, an empty table is shown
            and an optional info message is rendered.
        key_prefix: Unique key prefix for the grid instance (used by Streamlit state).
        empty_info: Optional info message to show when ``df`` is ``None`` or empty.
        component_source: Selected component source shown in the table toolbar.
        component_source_state_key: Session-state key updated when the source
            selector in the table toolbar changes.

    Returns:
        Streamlit components are rendered directly.
    """
    safe_df = df if (df is not None and not df.empty) else pd.DataFrame()
    display_df = _round_numeric_columns(safe_df)
    selected_source = tables.aggrid_table(
        display_df,
        key_prefix=key_prefix,
        download_file_name=f"{key_prefix}.csv",
        component_source=component_source,
    )

    if (
        component_source_state_key
        and selected_source
        and selected_source != component_source
    ):
        st.session_state[component_source_state_key] = selected_source
        st.rerun()

    if (df is None or df.empty) and empty_info:
        st.info(empty_info)
